name: Amram
overview: Amram is a male figure identified as a descendant of Bani who had married a foreign wife, as noted in Ezra 10:34. There is no specific tribal affiliation or additional personal notes recorded about him in Scripture beyond this unique attribute.
namesAndTitles: The name Amram means 'exalted people' and is a proper name mentioned in Ezra 10:34. There is no indication that this name was given by God, but it reflects a meaningful Hebrew designation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Amram as a descendant of Bani, establishing a direct familial link. No other family relationships are documented beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Amram's significance in the biblical narrative is tied to his status as a descendant of Bani who married a foreign wife, an issue addressed in Ezra 10:34 during the post-exilic period. His mention highlights the challenges faced by the returned exiles in maintaining covenantal purity and obedience to God's commands regarding marriage. This underscores the broader theme of faithfulness and holiness among God's people after the exile.
